notes: POC focused on tool-calling surface: create/update tickets in their proprietary ticket API + refund initiation to payments connector.
Primary ask: agent-assist that can call internal APIs safely (idempotent ticket create, attach transcripts, escalate to L4).
Performance targets: 95th perc latency < 300ms for agent-assist responses; burst throughput up to 450 reqs/min during peak campaigns.
Cost sensitivity: high — will trade model size vs tile economics. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching + quant profiles.
Security: must pass SOC2-equivalent questionnaire, SAML SSO, KMS for secrets; audit logs per ticket action for 1 year, redaction for PII in transcripts.
Refund flow: 2-step confirmation required (agent prompt + 2FA code) — cannot auto-finalize refunds without 2FA. Backend requires idempotency token to avoid double refunds.
Tool-calling requirements: webhook retry policy, guaranteed-at-least-once semantics OK but client prefers at-most-once for monetary ops -> need idempotency support in Redwood tool-calls.
Fallbacks: on model/latency degradation, traffic should fall back to lightweight hosted policy or stubbed responses, then to human escalation queue.
"We need deterministic ticket summaries for CSAT and downstream analytics" — customer repeated on 2026-02-12 call (fireflies ff_2026-02-12_03x9q7).
Integration targets: internal ticket service (api.cobalt.tickets/v1), payments gateway (stripe internal connector), and Workday for agent roster sync.
POC scope: 3-week sandbox, 1 end-to-end scenario (refund via agent-assist), 2 failure scenarios (API down, wrong idempotency token), measure error rates and mean time to resolution.
